ON 10.10.2024, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA NO. 19 OF 2021 2  2024:KER:75741  JUDGMENT
The claimant in O.P.(MV)No.229 of 2016 before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Punalur, is the appellant herein.
2. The facts for the disposal of the case are as follows:-

On 28.12.2015, at about 8 a.m, while the claimant was walking through the Kottarakkara-Kottayam M.C. Road, from north to south direction and when she reached near HP pumb, Kalayapuram, she was hit by a delivery van bearing Reg.No.KL-01 BK-8922 insured with the Director of Kerala State Insurance Department.
A claim was lodged before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal wherein the 1st respondent, the Director of Health Services and the 2 nd respondent, the driver, ex parte.

The 3rd respondent, Director of Kerala State Insurance Department entered appearance and contested the 2024:KER:75741 claim stating that it was due to the negligence of the claimant/appellant, the accident occurred.
On behalf of the claimant, Exts.A1 to A20 and Ext.X1 were marked.
X1 is the disability certificate issued by the Medical Board, Govt. Medical College Hospital, Thiruvananthapuram.
The claimant contented that the she was working as a cashew factory worker and she was earning Rs.9000/- per month.
However the tribunal awarded only Rs. 6000/- towards the monthly income.
Accordingly, the tribunal proceeded to grant the compensation as follows:-

Extra nourishment 10000 20000 2024:KER:75741 4 Damages to clothing 2000 2000 and articles
5 Medical expense and 73000 8195 (for medical bystanders' expense 26950 expenses) (77*350) 6 Compensation for pain 250000 150000 and sufferings 7
Compensation for 700000 460800 (6000*12*16*4) and loss of earning power 8 Compensation for loss 300000 200000 of amenities not Compensation for claimed future treatment Total 1500000 918945 3.
Heard Sri. Anchal C. Vijayan, the learned counsel for the appellant and Smt. Reshmi K.M, learned Senior Government Pleader for the 3rd respondent.
4. The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the claimant was having a monthly income of 2024:KER:75741 Rs.9000/-.

At any rate, she was entitled to have her notional income fixed in terms of the judgment of the Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd. [AIR 2011 SC 2951].

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel also pointed out with reference to the nature of injuries suffered by the appellant, the tribunal erred in fixing the functional disability based on X1.

In other words it is the specific contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that though the Medical Board has assessed 40% of disability, since severe injury to the brain was caused due to the accident, the tribunal ought to have taken a better percentage of functional disability and rather than fixing a disability at 40%.

It is further pointed out that even Indira vs The Additional Director, Directorate ... on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6328318/
2 though the claimant had only claimed Rs.9000/- as monthly income, nothing prevented the tribunal from since the same is imparted from 2024:KER:75741 the principles laid down by the Honorable Supreme court in Ramachandrappa (Supra).
5. On the other hand, Smt. Reshmi K.M, the learned Government Pleader appearing on the behalf of the State Insurance Department, opposed the plea of the appellant pointing that there was no evidence to show that the claimant was having an income of more than Rs.6000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Even though Ext.
A17 salary certificate was produced the same not proved by examining the employer who issued the same.

However despite this infirmity the tribunal accepted the same and therefore will not be permissible for this Court to deviate from the same and fix the notional income in terms of the principles laid down by the Honorable Supreme court in Ramachandrappa (Supra).
6.
I have considered the rival submissions raised 2024:KER:75741 across the Bar and I am perused the award.

7. No doubt the Honorable Apex court has laid down certain guiding principles for the Court and tribunals to fix the notional income while deciding a claim under Section 166 of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

However in a given case, when there is evidence to substantiate the claim of a monthly salary drawn by the claimant before the tribunal, can it be said that the principles laid down by the Ramachandrappa (Supra) would even then apply and the claimants are entitled to have the notional income fixed in accordance with the same.
The very purpose of fixation of notional income is that, in a given case where it is not possible for the claimant to prove that he or she is drawing such a monthly income.

However on contrary, in the facts of the case, Ext.A17 evidences that the claimant was drawing a 2024:KER:75741 monthly income of Rs.6000/- and therefore it is not possible for this Court to accept the argument of the appellant that the tribunal ought to have fixed an income more than what is reflected under Ext.A17.
Therefore, this Court is on considered view that there is considerable force in contention raised by the learned Senior Government pleader.
8. However, having said so, considering the nature of injury, this Court is of the considered view that the tribunal ought have fixed a higher percentage of functional disability.

The question as to whether the courts or the tribunals can fix higher percentage of disability as already been considered by the Supreme Court in Rekha Jain v. Natioanl Insurance Co.Ltd. (2013 KHC 4600).

entities.text: Rekha Jain v. Natioanl Insurance Co.Ltd. (2013 KHC 4600)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein the Supreme court has specifically held that it is for the courts and tribunals to fix the functional disability based on the 2024:KER:75741 nature of the injuries as well as the avocation done by the claimants.
The perusal of the award impugned in the appeal shows that the tribunal has taken note of the following injuries caused to the appellant/claimant in the accident.

1. Traumatice brain injury 2. Acute SDH (frontal region)
3. Diffuse brain oedema 4. Haemorrhagic contusion Indira vs The Additional Director, Directorate ...

3
5. Multiple petechial haemerrhages noted on left hemepous 6.
Mid brain left cerebellar hemesphere left.
9. A close scrutiny of the aforesaid injury, no doubt, gives a clear impression that the same are serious in nature.
It has come out in evidence that for 77 days, the claimant was treated at ESI Hospital, Ezhukone and as well as in the Medical College Hospital, Thiruvananthapuram as in- patient.

Considering these facts and also considering the avocation done by the claimant, this Court is of the view that 2024:KER:75741 the percentage of functional disability has to be increased considerably.

Similarly, in the light of the seriousness of the injury, which is suffered by the appellant/ claimant and also in view of the fact that she being entitled to have an higher degree of functional disability fixed and further she is also entitled for future prospects.

10. In the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, this Court finds that it would be appropriate to fix 75% of the functional disability considering the serious injuries caused to the brain, as extracted above.
Apart from that, this Court is not inclined to enhance the monthly income in terms of the principles laid down by the Honorable Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa (supra).
As an upshot of the above discussions, the appellant is entitled to succeed.
The appeal is thus allowed.
The 2024:KER:75741 compensation to which the appellant is entitled to re fix the accordingly.

the High  Court  1 Loss of earning 160000 36000 12,000  (6000*6) (6000x8-  36000)
 2 Compensation for 700000 460800 4,03,200  permanent disability [(6000x12x16x  and loss of earning 75/100)-
 power 460800  Total 1500000 918945 4,15,200
In view of the above discussions, the appeal is allowed.

It is ordered that the claim of the appellant is entitled for an enhanced claim of Rs.4,15,200/- (Four lakh fifteen thousand and two hundred only)
with proportionate cost which will 2024:KER:75741 carry interest at 7% from the date of petition till realization.

The Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced compensation together with interest and proportionate costs within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this Indira vs The Additional Director, Directorate ...
